scope: owned primary browser identification and signaling

findings.title: Ordinary restoration misses real timeout and occurs too early for cancellation
findings.sourceEvidence: The only ordinary event6/restoration call is in incoming Stop handling. The genuine step deadline returns from executeObservedReplay and reaches finish/result/exit internally, without that incoming Stop. exit seals the producer but does not restore descriptors. Therefore the real timeout cut has no restoration receipt for the mandatory restored assertion. For public cancellation, Stop restores the wrapper immediately after invoking the listener, while original native settlement and owner close are still pending. Later primitive entries in that interval bypass the removed observer.
findings.impact: The timeout case cannot satisfy its own closure witness, and cancellation loses independent observation of later native entries during cleanup.
findings.smallestFix: Keep non-C6 behavior unchanged. For selected ordinary C6, retain native wrappers through actual pending settlement and original SDK close; restore exactly once at that existing terminal cleanup seam and drain its scalar acknowledgement before final producer seal/exit. Do not require a fabricated Stop for timeout or restore merely at Stop entry.

findings.title: Produced-sink assertions can export raw text on a redaction failure
findings.sourceEvidence: The new sink checks pass the actual diagnostic errorMessage and the complete original stderr string to AssertJ contains assertions before checking released-value absence. An assertion failure can render those actual strings into the test failure report. Thus the failure that these checks are meant to detect can copy sensitive sink contents into an additional persisted surface. The existing assertJoinedSinkAbsent helper instead asserts scalar booleans with fixed labels.
findings.impact: A missing marker, stderr mismatch, or failed redaction can expose raw sink contents through assertion reporting even though the intended evidence is numeric.
findings.smallestFix: Run scalar literal/encoded absence checks first and express marker, equality, and stderr-presence checks as boolean/count assertions with fixed sanitized descriptions. Never supply actual message, raw stderr, runtime identifiers, or file contents as assertion actual/expected values.

findings.title: Guided hook restoration is skipped when shutdown rejects or busy drain expires
findings.sourceEvidence: Selected C6 descriptors are restored only in the fulfilled stop promise branch after busy clears. The rejected branch only marks failure, and the busy-timeout branch returns before revRestore. The runtime weak tag is deleted immediately regardless. Original browser close can reject; runtime closeResources clears its other resources in finally but does not restore these test-installed option hooks. No later C6 teardown branch retries those descriptors.
findings.impact: Failed original shutdown leaves installed hook closures/native wrappers retained in the live owning worker and loses the ordinary stop-tag route for restoration. Keeping evidence alive is appropriate while cleanup is unconfirmed, but it does not establish eventual exact restoration.
findings.smallestFix: Keep one selected-runtime restoration task reachable through both fulfillment and rejection. Retain hooks until original dispatch actually settles, then attempt exact descriptor restoration on every terminal path; mark close/restoration failures sticky and separately. On bounded busy-drain failure, retain an explicit teardown retry rather than deleting the only selected runtime tag and abandoning restoration. Do not restore early or change the original stop result.

sourceObservations.assessment: The source hashes the pinned executable, excludes helper --type processes, matches profile device/inode to the actual SDK launch and selected runtime, requires exactly one worker-descendant primary, and rechecks process start identity before signaling. No whole-worker substitute found.

Unavailable fence records original close separately and retains UNKNOWN effects rather than crediting zero writes. C6 still independently checks native closure, producer sealing, sticky failure flags and no next original native entry, subject to C6-PEER-01.

focus-enter starts the page request before synchronous stall, but its response processing and second page ack cannot execute until the stall exits or the realm is destroyed. The cut currently proves Java focus ingress plus an original Node active sample, not page receipt/completion of the focus ACK. Exact-seam wording requiring an acknowledged page focus event needs a precise disposition; no extra selector, value read or comparator is proposed.

Hooks attach through the existing real runtime options after selected start, compare the real released value only inside beforeSecretFill, and emit only transient raw-match scalars. Existing property-descriptor restoration support is reused. No production wire/config field was added.
